chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim raised it (as marfu') to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The seekers of knowledge are three — recognize them by their persons and their descriptions: a type who seeks it for ignorance and disputation, a type who seeks it for domination and deception, and a type who seeks it for understanding and intellect.

The one seeking it for ignorance and disputation is harmful and argumentative, exposing himself to speech in the assemblies of men by discussing knowledge while claiming the attribute of forbearance; he has clothed himself in humility while stripping himself of piety. May God crush his nose and cut off his chest.

The one seeking it for domination and deception is possessed of cunning and flattery — he dominates over those who resemble him, yet humbles himself before the wealthy beneath him. So he devours their worldly sweets while destroying his religion. May God blind his reputation and cut off his trace from the legacies of the scholars.

The one seeking it for understanding and intellect is possessed of grief, sorrow, and sleepless vigils — he has wrapped his cloak and stands the night in its darkness; he works and fears, trembling, supplicating, compassionate, attentive to his affairs, knowing the people of his time, wary even of his most trusted brethren. So may God strengthen his foundations and grant him security on the Day of Resurrection.

And it was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Mahmud Abu Abdillah al-Qazwini, from a number of our companions, among them Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sayqal in Qazwin, from Ahmad ibn Isa al-Alawi, from Abbad ibn Suhayb al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الِاسْتِطَالَة: Istitalah — seeking dominance or superiority over others through knowledge
key_terms.الْحِنْدِس: Hindis — pitch darkness, used poetically for the dark of night
key_terms.الْخَتْل: Khatal — guile, deception, seeking to manipulate others
key_terms.الْمِرَاء: Miraa' — contentious disputation, arguing for the sake of winning rather than truth
key_terms.الْوَرَع: Wara' — scrupulous piety, abstaining even from permissible things out of caution
key_terms.حَيْزُومَهُ: Hayzum — the chest and heart, site of intention; cutting it off means removing all motivation

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of knowledge seekers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) classifies all knowledge-seekers into three types based on their true intention: those driven by arrogance and love of debate (condemned), those driven by social climbing and manipulation (condemned), and those driven by genuine understanding and God-consciousness (praised). This typology was directed to students of religious learning in 8th-century Kufa and Medina, where scholarship had become intertwined with social prestige and court politics. The Imam's vivid characterizations — from the hypocritical debater clothed in false humility, to the genuinely devout scholar who distrusts even his closest companions — taught disciples to examine their own motivations for seeking knowledge.
